I'm thinking we should switch to the following (expanding on the discussion in email):

- Field - contiguous set of bits in an encoding (e.g., rs1, imm12_hi, imm12_lo)
- Opcode - A field that has a fixed value in an instruction (e.g., funct3)
- Operand - A potentially non-contiguous set of bits in the encoding (e.g., xs1, imm12), along with an ordering (e.g., 31|25-20|...), transformations (e.g., left_shift), types (e.g., X source reg), and relocations (e.g., REL_PC_HI)

Instruction formats are non-overlapping collections of one or more opcodes and zero or more operands.

Instruction types are non-overlapping collections of fields.

Instruction formats point to an instruction type, but don't go on to use anything from it (it's a suggestion, not a rule). We can talk about this later, but my finding is that we will wind up with a lot of types if we make it a rule.

Obviously, this change (or whatever we settle on) needs to happen before this PR.
